newsitem.title: USA: Campbell Soup launches home-delivered meals.
newsitem.headline: Campbell Soup launches home-delivered meals.

text.p: Campbell Soup Co said it began test marketing in Ohio Tuesday a new line of convenience meals that can be shipped to people with high blood pressure, high blood cholesterol and one type of diabetes.
For about $10 a day, a week's worth of breakfasts, lunches, dinners and snacks will be shipped via parcel service to customers' homes, Campbell said in a news release. Most of the meals are frozen.

The Intelligent Quisine program will be test marketed statewide in Ohio, the Camden, N.J.-based maker of Campbell, Pepperidge Farm and Swanson brand products said. Interested customers in Ohio are asked to call 1-800-220-2616.

The meal program was developed in conjunction with the American Heart Association and American Diabetes Association to meet dietary needs of 60 million American adults with those health concerns, including Type II diabetes, Campbell said.

"This program provides convenience to the consumer by delivering nutritious meals directly to their home," David Macnair, vice president and general manager of Campbell's Center for Nutrition & Wellness, said in the news release.
Entrees include grilled chicken dijon and French toast with sausage. Snacks include popcorn and peanut butter bars.
Customers incorporate their own fresh fruits, vegetables and low-fat dairy products, Campbell said.

Customers can call a toll-free hotline for individual nutrition counseling with a registered dietician, and Campbell will also provide newsletters and videotapes on exercise, nutrition and behavior modification.
In clinical tests of 800 people at eight North American university medical centers, the program reduced blood cholesterol blood pressure blood sugar in most participants, Campbell said.
